[PSL (NeurIPS 2024)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2411.00163) directly addresses the concern: softmax’s exponential weighting can let high-scoring false negatives dominate training. Its pairwise reformulation replaces the exponential with alternative activations, improving robustness and the connection to ranking metrics. This supports testing a less aggressively weighted objective on the existing GRU4Rec backbone; simply replacing BPR-max with ordinary sampled softmax does not resolve uncertain-negative amplification.

[Correcting the LogQ Correction (RecSys 2025)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.09331) revisits sampled-softmax bias: the positive is always included, whereas negatives are sampled. Its refined correction accounts for that distinction and introduces a model-uncertainty weight. This corrects sampling bias; it does not establish whether an unseen item is disliked. [Context-Aware Negative Sampling (2025)](https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/abstract/document/11021640) additionally shows context changes item distributions, but reports diversity gains with a small accuracy loss—no assurance of improved HR@10.

For this experiment, the strongest actionable hypothesis is a single GRU4Rec trained with PSL-style bounded negative influence, compared against sampling-corrected softmax using a known uniform/popularity proposal. These are proposed transfers, not demonstrated improvements on the four Amazon categories. Exclude known training positives from negative candidates; treat remaining false-negative confidence as a heuristic because exposure is unobserved. Electronics’ supplied 9.7% wrong-order rate measures ordering errors, not verified false negatives. Select exclusively by fixed macro validation HR@10; larger training margins alone provide no evidence of improvement.
